chunks.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْوَلِيدِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى الْعَطَّارُ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy upon him) narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from one of his companions from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: الْمُؤْمِنُ أَصْدَقُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ مِنْ سَبْعِينَ مُؤْمِنًا عَلَيْهِ

translations.en: The believer is more truthful with himself than seventy believers are with him.

en.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Sifat al-Shia*, this hadith*, this narration underscores the critical Shia concept of *muhasabah* (self-accountability), positing that a believer’s introspective honesty surpasses the external judgment of seventy others. This emphasizes that true piety (*taqwa*) begins with rigorous self-scrutiny before one is scrutinized by the community or God.
en.seo_question: What does it mean for a believer to be more truthful with himself than others?
